description: C++ Control Flow Practice: if-else, switch, loops, break and continue

questions.questionText: Which statement is used to execute a block of code only when a condition is true?
questions.explanation: The if statement executes its block when the specified condition evaluates to true.

questions.questionText: Which statement provides an alternative block when an if condition is false?
questions.explanation: The else block executes when the associated if condition is false.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int x = 7; if (x % 2 == 0) cout << "Even"; else cout << "Odd";
questions.explanation: 7 % 2 is 1, so the condition is false and Odd is printed.

questions.questionText: What is a nested if statement?
questions.optionA: An if statement without a condition
questions.optionC: An if statement inside another if statement
questions.optionD: An if statement inside a loop only
questions.explanation: A nested if is an if statement placed inside another if or else block.

questions.questionText: Which statement is useful when one expression needs to be compared with multiple constant values?
questions.explanation: The switch statement is useful for selecting among multiple constant cases.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to define an individual option inside a switch statement?
questions.explanation: The case keyword defines a possible value in a switch statement.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is commonly used to stop execution from falling through to the next case in a switch statement?
questions.explanation: The break statement exits the switch statement and prevents execution of subsequent cases.

questions.questionText: Which label executes when none of the specified switch cases match?
questions.explanation: The default label is executed when no case matches the switch expression.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int n = 2; switch(n) { case 1: cout << "A"; break; case 2: cout << "B"; break; default: cout << "C"; }
questions.explanation: n is 2, so case 2 executes and prints B.

questions.questionText: Which loop is generally preferred when the number of iterations is known beforehand?
questions.explanation: A for loop is commonly used when the initialization, condition and update are known.

questions.questionText: Which loop checks its condition before executing its body?
questions.explanation: Both while and for loops are entry-controlled loops and check their conditions before execution.

questions.questionText: Which loop guarantees that its body executes at least once?
questions.explanation: A do-while loop executes its body before checking the condition.

questions.questionText: What is the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) cout << i;
questions.explanation: The loop runs for i = 1, 2 and 3, so it prints 123.

questions.questionText: How many times does this loop execute? for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++)
questions.explanation: The values of i are 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4, so the loop executes 5 times.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int i = 1; while (i <= 3) { cout << i; i++; }
questions.explanation: The loop prints 1, 2 and 3 before i becomes 4.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int i = 1; do { cout << i; i++; } while (i <= 3);
questions.explanation: The do-while loop prints 1, 2 and 3.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int i = 5; while (i < 5) { cout << i; }
questions.explanation: The condition i < 5 is false initially, so the while loop body does not execute.

questions.questionText: Which statement immediately terminates the nearest loop or switch statement?
questions.explanation: The break statement immediately terminates the nearest enclosing loop or switch.

questions.questionText: Which statement skips the remaining statements of the current loop iteration and starts the next iteration?
questions.explanation: The continue statement skips the remaining part of the current iteration.

questions.questionText: What is the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i == 3) continue; cout << i; }
questions.explanation: When i is 3, continue skips cout, so the output is 1245.

questions.questionText: What is the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i == 3) break; cout << i; }
questions.explanation: When i becomes 3, break terminates the loop. Therefore, only 1 and 2 are printed.

questions.questionText: What is the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= 2; j++) cout << j; }
questions.explanation: The inner loop prints 12 three times, producing 121212.

questions.questionText: Which type of loop is called an entry-controlled loop?
questions.explanation: Both while and for check their conditions before executing the loop body.

questions.questionText: What happens if the condition of a while loop never becomes false?
questions.explanation: If the loop condition remains true and there is no terminating mechanism, the loop continues indefinitely.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int x = 2; if (x > 0) { if (x == 2) cout << "Two"; else cout << "Positive"; }
questions.explanation: x is greater than 0 and is exactly 2, so the nested if prints Two.
